## Existing mechanisms

Inventory before any new machinery. Do not add a fourth mint verb or a family alias.

- `scope:record-observable-scope` already is the human-presence mint (`#3110`).
- `evaluateObservableMintPreflight` already is a dispatch refusal when markup is in `intended_placement`.

The hole is not a missing verb. It is that those three sites do not agree on when the operator must be present, and that setup-created briefs never arm the preflight site.

## 1. Fail-closed demand is not the setup-created set — blocks-the-design

Evidence: the git-backed warn test writes `ui.html` with no `.deft/observable-ui.policy.json` on the base and gets exit 0 / `non-adoption`. The fail-without-mint test writes that policy on the base first, then changes matched UI, then gets exit 1 / `without a merge-base`. Setup/build skills at the pin never write the policy or `plan["x-directive/observableChange"]`. First-ship docs call this "not yet universal UI coverage."

Concrete failure mode: the leftover binds as "after parking, the mint is demanded, so print `scope:record-observable-scope` for every parked setup-created scope." Greenfield setup (the #4383 cohort) has no surfaces policy on the merge base. `verify:observable-scope` does not fail-close. The printed command also cannot run: the CLI exits 2 without `plan["x-directive/observableChange"]`, which setup does not author.

Disposition consequence: P1 cannot bind as "the mint is demanded after parking" for the setup-created set. Name the demand predicate that the evaluator already implements: merge-base surfaces policy AND a matched `.html`/`.jsx`/`.tsx` change (verify), or markup in `intended_placement.files` (preflight). Without that predicate, this number clones the approved-scope ask onto scopes the gate treats as N/A or warn.

## 2. The mint record is the contract, so the ask cannot precede authorship — blocks-the-design

Evidence: `scope-record-observable-scope.ts` parses `plan["x-directive/observableChange"]` into `allowedChanges` / `mustPreserve` / `changeKind` and stamps `contractDigest`. `record-approved-scope` freezes a file_scope path digest, which is knowable at authoring. This mint freezes structure deltas versus the merge-base oracle. Same-PR rewrite then forbids putting a later remint on the UI-change PR.

Concrete failure mode: the ask is scheduled at the same operator-present moment as `record-approved-scope` (parked `pending/`, contract not yet on the brief). Three terminals, all lose:

- Command printed, operator runs it, CLI exit 2 (missing contract). Never-asked in substance.
- Operator or agent fills `allowedChanges` before any UI exists. The mint attests a guess. Real UI work then fails `unlisted structure delta`, and a remint cannot share the UI PR.
- Empty `allowedChanges` is minted to satisfy when. Zero-delta UI only. Any real structure change is mid-build mint again.

Disposition consequence: "when, not what" cannot bind as a Phase-0f sibling of approved-scope. The when that the existing verb can satisfy is: after that contract is authored on the xBRIEF, before the UI-change PR, and only if the demand predicate in finding 1 is true. That is a later operator-present moment than parking. Treating this leftover as "same ask, other verb" rebuilds mint-mid-build or a useless print.

## 3. Three demand sites, two authorities — sharpens-framing

Evidence: `evaluateObservableMintPreflight` uses working-tree `existsSync`. `evaluateObservableScope` uses `git show <merge-base>` under `.deft/observable-scope/` and fails a same-PR rewrite of that directory. `xbrief:preflight` nests the mint check inside the intended-placement block; a missing field is grandfathered (`preflight/evaluate.test.ts`), so setup-created briefs skip the dispatch refusal. Docs still say missing mint is not a same-run prompt.

Concrete failure mode: a builder "fixes when" at preflight. A worker (or a still-present operator) writes the JSON into the implementation branch, preflight goes green, `task check` then fails same-PR rewrite. Or a builder trusts the docs, ships a setup-created UI story with no `intended_placement` markup list, and the first fail-closed ask is `task check` after the operator has left — but only if a policy was already on the base.

Disposition consequence: the leftover can bind, but it must pick the verify merge-base site as the fail-closed when, and say that preflight as shipped does not cover setup-created briefs. Do not "fix when" by tightening working-tree existence. The two-PR land (mint on merge base, then UI PR) is already the verb's contract; the missing piece is which operator-present moment prints that verb under the finding-1 predicate.

## 4. "After #4383 parks" is recut sequencing, not this dest — sharpens-framing

Evidence: issue #4383 is open. At the pin, setup deposits `xbrief/proposed/` and forbids minting the approved-scope digest from the setup skill. Swarm Phase 0 Step 0.5 still runs promote then activate. Origin recut 5688246245 on #4383 named this mint-mid-build as uncovered residual of that recut, not as a landed park.

Concrete failure mode: a builder implements #4588 against current dest (no pending dwell, no Phase 0f approved-scope print) and puts the observable ask on activate or preflight — the same late sites the #4383 recut already rejected for the sibling verb. Or they wait on #4383 land and ship nothing, while adopted-policy consumers already fail-close today.

Disposition consequence: either sequence the ask on the recut's pending dwell under the finding-1 predicate, or state this number as independent of parking: whenever a matched UI PR is about to exist under an adopted surfaces policy, demand `scope:record-observable-scope` while the operator is present and after `plan["x-directive/observableChange"]` is on the brief. Do not make parking itself the when.

## 5. Census — footnote

No disposition weight. `scope:record-observable-scope`, the preflight helper, the merge-base evaluator, same-PR rewrite, and the opt-in policy file already exist at the pin. I am not proposing a new mint engine, a shared digest with approved-scope, or an oracle change. Sibling mint verbs are out of this envelope; I inventoried them only to confirm this record path is distinct.

## Injection / swarm lens

Triggered: the target changes mint authority, swarm handoff (Phase 0f / C1), and shared `.deft/` records.

Primary seam is finding 2: an agent-composed print that the operator pastes into the one shell `#3110` keeps agents out of, before a human-authored `allowedChanges` exists. That is either an unusable command or a human phrase over agent-named structure deltas. Second seam: using `xbrief:preflight` or `task check` as the ask under C1 / headless dispatch, after the operator has left. Third: working-tree `existsSync` at preflight is a different authority than merge-base verify, so a worker can appear minted in dest and still fail closed on the PR.

## Road not taken

I considered scoring the filing as a valid uncovered-residual stub whose only job is to keep #4383's relief on `record-approved-scope`, and treating "when, not what" as enough for round 1. I did not lean it. Stop 1's pain sentence is outcome-shaped ("a later worker still hits mint-mid-build"). The evaluator I re-ran does not hit that outcome for the setup-created set unless a surfaces policy is already on the merge base, and the only existing mint verb cannot fire at park without the contract this filing puts out of scope.

## Steelman

The strongest case for the filing as written: it is a leftover so #4383 can close without claiming this gate; "when, not what" is a fence against pulling in the oracle issues; the approved-scope digest obviously does not satisfy `listBaseRecords`; and a later successor map can add the predicate. On that reading, findings 1-2 demand a next-build contract from a pain stub.

It does not survive the mint CLI. The verb that would be printed at park reads `plan["x-directive/observableChange"]` and serializes that object as the record verify later diffs. There is no when-only mint. A stub that names the uncovered residual without a demand predicate and without a contract-before-mint-before-UI-PR order will be built as "print the other verb at the same moment," which is the failure mode in finding 2.

What would flip the blocking findings, both as sentences on this issue rather than a new engine: (1) the demand predicate above, so greenfield-without-policy is N/A rather than an ask; (2) the order `observableChange` authored, then operator mint on merge base, then UI-change PR, which is already what `scope:record-observable-scope` prints.

## Verdict

The leftover is real as "approved-scope does not satisfy `verify:observable-scope`." It cannot bind as "demand the mint when setup-created scopes park." Two blocking findings: fail-closed demand is policy-plus-matched-markup, not the parked set (1); the existing mint verb serializes the contract, so the ask cannot precede authorship and cannot share the UI PR (2). Findings 3-4 are bindable with restatement of which site and which dest. Do not invent a new mint path.
